rationale: Evidence from iteration 2 (score 475.9, the best so far). The oval now finishes 20/20 in 1.69 s with 0.15 line-loss events and max_error 0.040 m, so the controller works on gentle curves and the speed is sufficient there. The s-bend finishes 5/20 (progress 0.67) and the slalom finishes 0/20 (progress 0.16). Both failing tracks end off track with about one line-loss event per run. The likely cause is that base_speed 1.2 is too fast for the sharp transitions, so the robot leaves the tape before the steering can correct. Geometry cannot fix this: the off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which stays at 0.06 for any body width up to about 0.19 m. Changes: base_speed 1.2 to 1.0, with all geometry and the other gains (kp 2.2, ki 0.15, kd 0.8) held fixed so the effect is isolated. Expected result: the s-bend finish rate rises above 0.5 and slalom progress rises above 0.3. The oval still finishes at about 2.0 s, which costs roughly 6 points of time score but gains completions worth 500 each. Hypotheses for the next race: H1, speed is the main cause of the s-bend and slalom departures; H2, if the slalom still fails early, steering authority at the sharp alternations is the limit and kp needs revisiting; H3, steering_oscillation stays near 0.2 to 0.3 because of sensor quantisation, and kd is already adequate. Next measurements: completion and completion_time on the s-bend, progress and line_loss_events on the slalom, and max_error and steering_oscillation on all tracks.
